Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.

Question: What is the occupation of Jean Auclair?
Document 1: As the sun set over the charming streets of Lyon, Jean Auclair made his way through the winding alleys, his worn leather satchel slung over his shoulder. The scent of freshly baked croissants wafted from the nearby patisserie, enticing him to stop for a quick breakfast before his shift at the Hôpital Édouard Herriot. Jean's eyes, a deep shade of indigo, sparkled with a quiet intensity as he pushed open the door to the hospital's staff entrance. Inside, the bustling corridors were a familiar comfort, a world away from the cutthroat arena of French politics he had once navigated. Few would recognize the former député, known for his impassioned speeches and sharp wit, in the humble, scrubs-clad figure now expertly juggling a tray of medications and a steaming cup of coffee. As he made his way to the nurses' station, Jean exchanged warm bonjours with his colleagues, his French accent infusing the hospital's sterile air with a touch of warmth. His supervisor, the no-nonsense Madame Dupont, nodded in approval as he began to review the morning's patient charts. "Bonjour, Jean. I see you're on top of things as usual. You're a natural with our patients." Jean's lips curved into a gentle smile, his eyes crinkling at the corners. It was a far cry from the high-stakes world of politics, where every word was a calculated move, every gesture a carefully crafted image. Here, among the beeping machines and antiseptic smells, he was free to be himself – a licensed practical nurse, dedicated to the simple, yet profound, act of caring for others. As he began his rounds, Jean's hands moved with a quiet confidence, his touch gentle yet firm as he checked vital signs and administered medications. It was a skill honed over years of dedication, a testament to the quiet strength that lay beneath the polished façade of the politician he once was.
Document 2: Title: The Unlikely Politician: Jean Auclair's Journey from Politics to Pension

In the quaint town of Lyon, France, a peculiar sight could be seen strolling along the Rhône River. Jean Auclair, a former French politician, had traded in his suit and tie for a more relaxed attire, often accompanied by a gentle smile and a twinkle in his eye. The once-bustling corridors of the National Assembly now seemed a distant memory, replaced by the tranquil atmosphere of his favorite café, where he would spend hours sipping coffee and reminiscing about his past. As a seasoned politician, Jean had dedicated his life to serving the people of France. He had been a vocal advocate for social justice, fighting tirelessly to improve the lives of the working class. His unwavering commitment had earned him the respect of his peers and the admiration of his constituents. However, after decades of service, Jean had decided it was time to hang up his political boots and enjoy the fruits of his labor. The evidence of Jean's new life as a pensioner was evident in the way he carried himself. Gone were the days of hurried meetings and late-night parliamentary sessions. Instead, he had adopted a leisurely pace, taking pleasure in the simple things. His mornings began with a gentle stroll, followed by a visit to the local market, where he would engage in lively conversations with the vendors and sample the freshest produce. Jean's pension, earned after years of dedicated service, provided him with the financial security to pursue his passions without the burden of a 9-to-5 job. He had always been an avid reader, and now he had the time to devour books on history, philosophy, and literature. His love for reading had become so pronounced that he had even started a book club in his community, where he would lead discussions and debates with fellow retirees. The pensioner's life had also given Jean the opportunity to reconnect with his family and friends. He would often host dinner parties, regaling his guests with stories of his time in politics and sharing his wisdom gained from years of experience. His grandchildren would visit him regularly, and he would take them on walks along the river, teaching them about the importance of social responsibility and the value of hard work.
